harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 with the given SSH public key, enforced key-only SSH authentication cluster-wide via sshd_config.d, verified enforcement, then performed the mandatory single-node restart with proof of changed boot identity and full post-restart recovery of the SSH configuration and opsadmin access.
actions_performed: Checked baseline: opsadmin user did not exist; default sshd_config had PasswordAuthentication commented (default yes)
Created opsadmin user with home dir, .ssh/authorized_keys containing the required ed25519 public key, correct permissions (700/600) and ownership, and locked the password

Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-opsadmin-key-only.conf enforcing PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, ChallengeResponseAuthentication no, PermitRootLogin prohibit-password
Validated config with sshd -t and restarted sshd
Verified effective config via sshd -T shows password/kbd-interactive auth disabled and pubkey auth enabled
Functionally tested SSH: BatchMode connection without matching key was rejected via publickey/gssapi methods only, confirming no password prompt is offered
Captured baseline boot_id and service/user state prior to restart
Issued sudo systemctl reboot on node1 (ack observed via stream drop) and polled until exec access returned
Verified boot_id changed post-restart, confirming an actual reboot occurred
Re-verified sshd active, key-only auth policy still in effect, and opsadmin user/authorized_keys intact after restart

evidence.requirement: opsadmin user created with required SSH public key installed
evidence.summary: Confirmed opsadmin did not exist beforehand, created it and installed the exact public key into authorized_keys with correct ownership/permissions.

evidence.requirement: Key-based SSH authentication required (password/interactive auth disabled)
evidence.summary: Added and validated a drop-in sshd config disabling password and keyboard-interactive auth while keeping pubkey auth enabled; sshd -T confirms the effective runtime config; live SSH attempt without a matching key was rejected via publickey/gssapi only (no password prompt), proving enforcement.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id (377b5195...), sshd active status, and opsadmin/authorized_keys state prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Issued systemctl reboot (stream closed acknowledging the disruption), polled until node1 became reachable again, and confirmed boot_id changed to 6c62b7e8... with a fresh uptime -s timestamp, proving an actual reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: post-restart recovery of required services/state
evidence.summary: Post-reboot check shows sshd active, effective sshd -T policy still enforcing pubkey-only auth, and opsadmin user with its authorized_keys entry intact.
